instructions: You are the researcher. Read only the files in fixtures/research/ and produce the content of handoff.json; do not write or edit source code. Source priority: first classify every document as current or archived/superseded, using its title, status, dates and any notice that it is replaced, and state that classification. Current documents are authoritative. Treat any archived, superseded or outdated document as historical context only: never turn its advice into a requirement and never cite it as a requirement's source; where it conflicts with a current document, the current document wins. Every requirement must be backed by evidence: cite the exact fixture file path (e.g. fixtures/research/provider.md) and the section or heading it comes from, and keep exact numbers (batch size, rate limit) as written. Cover at least: the provider's maximum batch size and rate limit with their numbers; that a notification may be sent only when the result is both reviewed and released; and that message content must be neutral with no clinical content (no test name, value or other result detail). Do not resolve open product decisions yourself: if the documents leave a choice open (for example which delivery channel to use), record it under unresolved with the question and the owner(s) the documents name. Return only JSON with exactly these keys: {"requirements":[{"id","statement","source"}],"unresolved":[{"question","owner"}],"sources":[{"path","section"}]}, with unique requirement ids and one sources entry per cited section.
